evidence.title: Retraining on recommendation-influenced behavior can increase homogenization without utility gains
evidence.observation: Source-reported finding: In simulations, retraining recommenders on behavior shaped by earlier recommendations increases homogenization without corresponding utility improvement and changes consumption distributions. Observation period and measurement context: Discrete simulation steps with synthetic users/items; no real-world observation dates.
evidence.evidence_standing: Source-reported bounded account; Simulation study; not independently reproduced
evidence.glossary_fit: Illustrative or qualifying; does not validate a definition

source_locations.SRC-130: Current preprint PDF §§4, 5.2–5.4, 6 and version metadata

evidence.limitations: Simulated preferences, selected algorithms and one interaction per user per step limit transfer. Effects vary by algorithm; random recommendations provide a contrast. Population-level polarization was not measured.
evidence.open_questions: Transfer to other populations, tasks and operating environments remains unestablished. Missing measurement details are not inferred.
evidence.support_assessment: Commons interpretation: System-shaped observations feed back into training; no faster cycle is established.
evidence.dispute_status: See source version and dispute qualifications; no systematic clearance claimed.
evidence.verification_status: Not independently verified by the Commons

terms.name: Cross-system feedback
terms.definition: A pattern in which an action or output from one technical or organizational process affects activity elsewhere and subsequent responses modify conditions for additional participants. Many response paths may exist; there need not be a single linear loop.

terms.name: Feedback amplification
terms.definition: A feedback effect in which an activity and the reactions it generates increase the intensity, reach, amount, or consequences of subsequent activity. Stabilizing or dampening responses may limit or reverse amplification.
